title: The Ships of Death
sentences: Twelve ships sailed into a harbor in Sicily. Their crews were sick and dying.
It was October 1347, and the port was Messina.
The sick had painful black swellings, and most died within days.
The city ordered the ships back out to sea. It was already too late.
The disease was plague, caused by a bacterium called Yersinia pestis.
Within four years, it killed up to half the people in Europe.
It became one of the deadliest pandemics in recorded history.
Follow for more from the Black Death.
caption:
